rationale: A wins because it knows where the story can blow up: "whether the subscriptions flow through mobile in-app purchase at all" is the exact question that decides whether the 10%-vs-30% angle survives a real platform-fees reporter. B has good bones, but "right before an IPO" turns reported preparation into a calendar fact, and "Paying for the room, not the creator" leans on a category distinction the update does not prove. A is harder to embarrass.
gaps_in_A: "Discord takes 10% where Apple takes 30%" names Apple even though the update only gives a 30% app-store standard; the mobile billing path needs confirmation before that headline is safe.
"Discord is launching a creator payments business with no earnings data to show for it" risks treating a normal launch-day absence as a gotcha; A caveats it, but it is still the thinnest angle.

"Discord is turning 200 million users into a subscription business before an IPO" leans hard on MAU as a monetizable base and on IPO timing; the facts only say reportedly preparing and give no eligible-server count.
gaps_in_B: "right before an IPO" overstates "reportedly preparing" into a timing claim; a markets reporter will cut that down fast.
"Paying for the room, not the creator" depends on "rather than for an individual creator's content feed," a category claim not supplied by the update.
The fee angle's proof list asks about processing and permanence but misses the killer question: whether iOS or Android purchases route through app-store billing and stack another commission.
"the person who has run a large gaming community for free" invents the unpaid-volunteer setup; plausible is not the same as grounded.
